To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the old-growth forests have a higher species richness and abundance than the managed forests, that several species and genera are strong indicators of old-growth forests and that lichens with vegetative reproduction are more frequent in managed forests.
lichens are good indicators of forest quality and that they can be used for the evaluation of forest management.
the lichen diversity is significantly higher and the species composition is different in old-growth mountain spruce forests than in managed spruce forests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of old-growth forests for biodiversity and their role as a refuge for lichen species in the Czech Republic.
the conservation and restoration of old-growth forests, which should include the preservation of lichen diversity and composition.
the assessment and evaluation of the lichen biodiversity in old-growth spruce forests in mountain ranges of the Czech Republic and its relation to managed forests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lichen communities of natural mountain spruce forests are characterized by higher species richness and abundance of species, higher number of Red-list species, higher diversity of functional traits, higher functional, taxonomic, and phylogenetic diversity.
the lichen communities of managed forests are less diverse, species-poor and less representative than those of old-growth forests, but the differences are relatively small.
the old-growth forests have a higher species richness and diversity of lichens, and that the managed forests can be characterized by a higher abundance, but lower diversity of lichen species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lichens can be used to assess biodiversity and quality in old-growth mountain spruce forests.
the natural mountain spruce forests of the Czech Republic are the most important lichen habitats and should be protected.

lichen species richness is higher in old-growth spruce forests and that lichens with vegetative reproduction, stalked apothecial, pigmented ascosopores and large ascosopores may be used as indicator species of old-growth forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the old-growth mountain forests of the Czech Republic are important biodiversity hotspots and should be protected.
old-growth forests should be protected in nature conservation and that the management of spruce forests should consider the conservation of old-growth forests.
lichens can provide useful indicators for old-growth forest quality and can be used in nature conservation.
